$comment: Volt Lighting (landscape and outdoor lighting, sold direct) runs a custom storefront with product pages at the top level (for example /mr11-decorative-rock-light). The product name is the h1, the description is the meta description and the image is og:image. The price ($33.99 on the sample) is in the page's schema.org Product JSON-LD and the rendered price block; the specifications (lumens, IP rating, warranty, finish) are in tabs the selectors cannot read. fetch.engine is default (APP_DEFAULT_ENGINE, ai-crawler-avalai on this instance): the LLM reads the JSON-LD price (3399 cents, available), 17 specs and 5 features, each checked against the page, at about 5,718+1,308 tokens per request. Engines tried on the sample on 2026-11-19: http: SUCCESS with title, image and description but no price; browser: the same; ai-crawler-avalai: SUCCESS with the price, 17 specs and 5 features; web_search: success but unverified. ai-crawler-avalai is selected because it returns the price and the specs. Needs APP_AI_CRAWLER_ENABLED with an AvalAI key on the instance. Checked against the saved (curl) MR11 Decorative Rock Light page on 2026-11-19. The /shop listing page also matches the single-segment product pattern (it is not fetched as a product in production because the product pages are reached from the catalogue).
